mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY growth < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 8% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which compresses earnings for cyclically-sensitive sectors and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary policy tightening coinciding with rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > 3% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline > 3% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that boosts wage pressure and input costs, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as companies in resilient sectors outperform.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo avg AND UNRATE < previous 12-mo avg
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month average and UNRATE is below its 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a recovery in manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings for cyclicals and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of INDPRO increases.
